JUDGMENT

SARDAR MUHAMMAD RAZA, J.â€‘â€‘â€‘ Vide judgment
and decree dated 25â€‘2â€‘1997, learned Judge Family Court, Peshawar
granted a decree for maintenance at the rate of rupees one thousand per month
in favour of Mst. Nusrat Begum and against her husband Abdul Jalil. The amount
of decree included past maintenance as well.

2. The husband went in appeal where: learned Additional
District Judge Peshawar directed him to affix courtâ€‘fees under section
7(2) of the Court Fees Act within a period fixed by the appellate Court. Such
courtâ€‘fee was not affixed in the given period and hence the appeal was
dismissed vide judgment dated 8â€‘10â€‘1998 and hence this petition
under Article 199 of the Constitution.

3. It is a settled law in the N.â€‘W. F. P. that a courtâ€‘fee
of rupee one is affixed on the plaint before a Family Court under section 19 of
the West Pakistan Family Court Act, 1964. The section specifically mentions the
word "plaint" which, therefore, would be deemed to have excluded the
memorandum of appeal. Such memorandum shall, therefore, be liable to â€‘be
affixed ad valorem courtâ€‘fee on the subject.â€‘matter of dispute, as
provided by section 7 of Court Fees Act.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent placed reliance upon a
judgment of the Honourable Supreme Court given in Mirza Daud Baig v. Additional
District Judge, Gujranwala 1987 SCMR 1161. All the principles governing the
affixation of courtâ€‘fees on plaint before a Civil Court and on plaint
before a Family Court and also on memorandum of appeal before the first
appellate Court are elaborately discussed in the light of section 7 of the
Court Fees Act and all relevant sections of the: Family Courts Act,. 1964. It
is observed that on memorandum of appeal the mode of valuation for the purpose
of courtâ€‘fee would be ten times the value of maintenance granted for a
period of one year. In the instant case, such valuation for the purposes of P
courtâ€‘fee amounted to Rs.120,000. The petitioner was given time by the
First Appellate Court to affix the courtâ€‘fee, which was not so affixed
and hence the appeal was rightly dismissed. The petitioner had availed
assistance of a counsel who could have calculated the same in the light of
section 7 of the Court Fees Act. The writ petition is hereby dismissed.

H.B.T./86/P Petition dismissed.
